bull.b: The large multiyear backlog provides substantial visibility into future module deliveries and revenue, reducing reliance on near-term spot demand. Scheduled commitments through 2030 also support production planning, capacity utilization, and confidence in medium-term cash-flow generation.

Very high gross and adjusted EBITDA margins demonstrate strong current earnings power and the benefits of First Solar’s U.S.-produced module mix. If maintained, this profitability can fund technology investment, capacity expansion, and resilience through demand or policy changes.

Extremely low leverage gives First Solar substantial financial flexibility and limits solvency pressure as it expands manufacturing and develops new technologies. Strong returns achieved without heavy debt indicate that the business can generate attractive profitability while preserving balance-sheet resilience.

bear.b: The sales decline and reduced full-year outlook indicate that recent earnings strength is not yet matched by consistent top-line momentum. Lower expected volumes can weaken operating leverage, complicate capacity planning, and make near-term results more dependent on product mix and pricing.

Recent cash generation has lagged reported earnings materially, creating a quality risk despite strong accounting profitability. Persistently weak conversion could reduce internally funded investment capacity, increase dependence on working-capital timing, and limit flexibility for growth or shareholder returns.

Unresolved trade rules can delay customer commitments and make module pricing, sourcing decisions, and project economics harder to establish. That uncertainty may extend sales cycles, moderate bookings, and create uneven utilization even while domestic manufacturing remains strategically advantaged.
